title: Ensemble pour la République march over governing politicians’ statements in Lubumbashi

organizer: Ensemble pour la République supporters/activists, including party youth members

title.summary: Opened reports describe an Ensemble pour la République march in Lubumbashi protesting remarks attributed to serving or governing-camp politicians.

start_date.summary: The two opened articles date the physical march to 19 January. A Radio Okapi search-result lead dates a similar march to 20 January; its body was inaccessible, so a one-day date conflict remains.

end_date.summary: The opened reports describe dispersal but do not establish a physical end time or later return.

location.summary: The opened accounts place the march in Lubumbashi; S040 says police dispersed it before the governor’s office.

scope.summary: The sources describe a city march in Lubumbashi.

organizer.summary: The march involved supporters/activists of Ensemble pour la République; S040 quotes a party youth official.

demands.summary: The sources describe protest against a minister’s or governing-camp politicians’ public statements characterized by organizers as separatist; political_behavior_process is provisional.

state_target.summary: S040 identifies serving hydrocarbons minister Didier Budimbu’s remarks; S045 reports that organizers planned a memorandum to the provincial governor. The grievance concerns public conduct of governing officials, not electoral support.

participants_original.summary: Enquete.cd reports “plusieurs milliers d’activistes”; this is qualitative, not converted into an exact count.

participants_min.summary: No exact minimum is reported; “several thousand” remains qualitative.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The opened report’s “several thousand activists” description clearly exceeds 50; no numeric bounds are derived.

protester_violence.summary: The opened accounts do not describe violence by march participants; unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Both opened accounts report police used tear gas to disperse the march.

state_response.arrests.summary: S040 attributes an arrest report to a party youth official; S045 says its sources reported no arrests. The claim is contested.

state_response.beatings.summary: S040 attributes an allegation that women and young people were beaten to a party youth official; S045 reports injuries but does not independently establish beatings.

state_response.killings.summary: Enquete.cd says its sources reported no deaths; this is source-attributed and not independently verified.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The opened articles do not report a government meeting or accommodation.

state_response.ignore.summary: No later government response to this march is established.

state_response.shootings.summary: The opened articles report tear gas but do not describe shooting.

eligibility.summary: The opened coverage supports physical assembly, qualitative attendance above 50, and a grievance over conduct by serving/governing officials. The report does not describe an exclusively electoral act of support; final codebook review remains pending.

notes: A party organized the march, but the opened accounts frame it as opposition to a serving minister’s/public governing-camp politicians’ statements and report a memorandum for the governor, rather than electoral support. Review against the original manual after the baseline gate. Keep the arrest and date conflicts explicit; qualitative turnout is not converted to bounds. S046/S047/S048/S049/S055 are search-only, with S049 Africa-Press remaining under the inherited publisher hold.
open_questions: Did the physical march occur on 19 January or 20 January, and are the reports about the same episode?

Does the original manual treat this government-conduct grievance as distinct from excluded partisan electoral mobilization?
What was the physical end of the march?
